classification.difficultyReason: Construct multi-step proofs using parallelogram properties, triangle congruence and converse parallel-angle facts.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Given that $ABCD$ is a parallelogram, prove that $AP=QC$.

spec.description: Parallelogram with P on AB, Q on DC, joins AQ and PC, and two 50-degree givens.
spec.mathematics: Angle DQA and angle BPC are 50 degrees. Single arrows pair AB with DC; double arrows pair AD with BC.

answer.short:
$AP=QC$.

Equal corresponding angles give $AQ\parallel PC$, so $APCQ$ is a parallelogram.
answer.worked: $\angle PAQ=\angle AQD=50^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$). Also $\angle BPC=50^\circ$ (given). Thus $\angle PAQ=\angle BPC$, so $AQ\parallel PC$ (equal corresponding angles). Since $AP\parallel QC$ as well, $APCQ$ is a parallelogram. Its opposite sides are equal, so $AP=QC$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Given that $RSTU$ is a parallelogram, prove that $UX\parallel YS$.

spec.description: Oblique parallelogram RSTU with X on RS, Y on UT, joins UX and YS, and double ticks on XS and UY.
spec.mathematics: XS=UY and XS is parallel to UY. Opposite outer sides have paired parallel arrows.
spec.answerVisibility: No requested parallelism marked on UX and YS.

answer.short:
$UX\parallel YS$.

$XS=UY$ and $XS\parallel UY$, so $XSYU$ is a parallelogram.
answer.worked: $XS\parallel UY$ because $RS\parallel UT$. Also $XS=UY$ (given). Thus $XSYU$ is a parallelogram, since one pair of opposite sides is equal and parallel. Its other pair of opposite sides is parallel, so $UX\parallel YS$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram with $X$ and $Y$ points on the diagonal $BD$ such that $BY=DX$. Prove that $AYCX$ is a parallelogram.

spec.description: Outer parallelogram, diagonal DB with D,X,Y,B in order, equal ticks on DX and YB, and dotted target quadrilateral.
spec.mathematics: BY=DX; both pairs of outer opposite sides are parallel.
spec.answerVisibility: No congruence or target-side equality supplied.

answer.short:
$AYCX$ is a parallelogram.

SAS congruence gives $AX=CY$ and $AY=CX$, so both pairs of opposite sides are equal.
answer.worked:
In triangles $ADX$ and $CBY$:
$$\begin{align*}AD&=CB &&\text{(opposite sides of a parallelogram)}\\DX&=BY &&\text{(given)}\\\angle ADX&=\angle CBY &&\text{(alternate angles, }AD\parallel BC\text{)}\end{align*}$$
Thus $\triangle ADX\equiv\triangle CBY$ (SAS), so $AX=CY$.

In triangles $ABY$ and $CDX$, $AB=CD$, $BY=DX$, and $\angle ABY=\angle CDX$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$). Therefore $\triangle ABY\equiv\triangle CDX$ (SAS), so $AY=CX$.

Both pairs of opposite sides of $AYCX$ are equal; hence $AYCX$ is a parallelogram.

children.label: d
children.prompt: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram and $PB=DQ$. Prove that $AQ=CP$.

spec.description: Parallelogram with D,P,Q,B in order on diagonal DB and joins AQ and PC.
spec.mathematics: PB=DQ is stated in the prompt; opposite outer sides are marked parallel.
spec.answerVisibility: AQ and CP are not marked equal.

answer.worked:
In triangles $ADQ$ and $CBP$:
$$\begin{align*}AD&=CB &&\text{(opposite sides of a parallelogram)}\\DQ&=BP &&\text{(given)}\\\angle ADQ&=\angle CBP &&\text{(alternate angles, }AD\parallel BC\text{)}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle ADQ\equiv\triangle CBP$ (SAS), so $AQ=CP$ (matching sides).

children.label: e
children.prompt: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram and $BX$ and $DY$ are perpendicular to $AC$. Prove that $BX=DY$.

spec.description: Parallelogram with diagonal AC and perpendiculars BX and DY; feet derived by projection onto AC.
spec.mathematics: A,X,Y,C are collinear in that order. Right-angle squares occur at X and Y; opposite sides have matching parallel arrows.
spec.answerVisibility: No equality marks on the perpendiculars.

answer.worked:
In triangles $ABX$ and $CDY$:
$$\begin{align*}AB&=CD &&\text{(opposite sides of a parallelogram)}\\\angle BAX&=\angle DCY &&\text{(alternate angles, }AB\parallel CD\text{)}\\\angle BXA&=\angle DYC=90^\circ &&\text{(given perpendiculars)}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle ABX\equiv\triangle CDY$ (AAS), so $BX=DY$ (matching sides).

children.label: f
children.prompt: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram with $BP=DQ$. Prove that $APCQ$ is a parallelogram.

spec.description: Parallelogram ABCD with P on AB, Q on DC, and joins AQ and PC.
spec.mathematics: BP=DQ is stated in the prompt. Double arrows pair AB with DC; single arrows pair AD with BC.

answer.short:
$APCQ$ is a parallelogram.

SAS congruence gives $AQ=CP$ and equal angles that establish $AQ\parallel PC$.
answer.worked:
In triangles $ADQ$ and $CBP$:
$$\begin{align*}AD&=CB &&\text{(opposite sides of a parallelogram)}\\DQ&=BP &&\text{(given)}\\\angle ADQ&=\angle CBP &&\text{(opposite angles of }ABCD\text{)}\end{align*}$$
Thus $\triangle ADQ\equiv\triangle CBP$ (SAS). Hence $AQ=CP$ and $\angle DQA=\angle BPC$ (matching parts).

Also $\angle BPC=\angle PCD$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel DC$). Therefore $\angle DQA=\angle PCD$, so $AQ\parallel PC$ (equal corresponding angles).

One pair of opposite sides of $APCQ$ is equal and parallel, so $APCQ$ is a parallelogram.
